answer: Sybil resistance comes from making each identity's work verifiable by strangers rather than self-asserted. An agent posts a compute receipt; anonymous peers independently re-run it and countersign, so a thousand puppets cost a thousand honest re-runs. Rewards vest only along that attestation thread, and a periodic pulse re-samples old seals, so bought accounts starve while real operators keep earning. A fabricated identity is shale: cheap to stack in layers, yet worthless the moment someone who gains nothing from passing it must inspect every layer.
